New genetic association datasets in the Knowledge Portals

In our most recent release, we added to the CMDKP 18 new datasets with associations for 23 traits, including the largest-to-date datasets for plasma lipid levels and kidney function measurements, 6 new datasets for liver function and disease, and datasets for renal and vascular diabetic complications. We also added datasets for reproductive traits (gestational diabetes and gestational weight gain), a new phenotype category for the CMDKP. We added to the Lung Disease Knowledge Portal four analyses of COVID-19 associations from the Round 6 freeze of the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative study. Find all the details on the latest release in this brief video, and stay tuned for our upcoming release in early June, which will feature the large (1.3 million subjects!) new DIAMANTE trans-ethnic meta-analysis of type 2 diabetes associations (Mahajan et al., 2022).

 

New effector lists

The Knowledge Portals now include two new lists of predicted effector genes: effectors for type 1 diabetes, generated by Kyle Gaulton and colleagues at UCSD (unpublished); and effectors for osteoarthritis, generated by the Genetics of Osteoarthritis consortium (Boer et al. 2021). We will be adding curated lists of predicted effectors for various traits and diseases on an ongoing basis. Contact us if you have generated a list that you would like to share on the Knowledge Portals!

New tool: Variant Sifter

The Variant Sifter is an in-development interactive tool that allows users to explore, filter, and prioritize genetically associated variants, credible sets, and tissue-specific epigenomic annotations across a region, providing decision support for prioritization of variants and genes for further research. Find it under the “KP Labs” menu on all the Knowledge Portals.

New portal: NAGEKP

Most genome-wide association studies test only the additive model for genetic association, missing associations for variants that follow non-additive inheritance models. In collaboration with Josep Mercader at the Broad Institute, we have created the new Non-Additive Genetic Effects Knowledge Portal (NAGEKP) to house non-additive results. Currently it includes non-additive associations for 22 age-related phenotypes (Guindo-Martínez et al., 2021), along with additive associations for related traits. Our June release will include a new dataset that includes recessive model associations for T2D (O'Connor et al., 2022).

New service: Bring Your Own Results (BYOR)

Recognizing a need among our collaborators to visualize their results quickly and easily, without having to have coding expertise, we have created the BYOR service. This open-access platform allows you to generate interactive tables and visualizations from a wide variety of scientific data types and post them on web pages to share privately or publicly. Find all the details here.

AMP® CMD news

The Accelerating Medicines Partnership® in Common Metabolic Diseases includes $500,000 annually in funding for projects that are aligned with the goals of the consortium. The combined first two years of funding have now been awarded to 4 projects that will create resources for functional characterization of genes potentially involved in metabolic disease. The next cycle of funding will be announced in early summer 2022. Watch the CMDKP home page or our Twitter feed (@AMP_CMDKP) for the announcement, and contact us with any questions.

Spotlight on AMP CMD scientists

We’ve started a news feature to introduce the scientists of AMP CMD. So far, we have featured Dr. Wenli Yang from the University of Pennsylvania and Dr. Aoife McMahon from EMBL-EBI. Read their profiles here.

CMDGA news

Did you know that you can access, explore, and download the large single-nucleus ATAC-seq dataset from Chiou et al. 2021 in the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA)? Use the new Gene Expression Browser to compare expression levels for genes of interest in multiple pancreatic and blood cell types in both dot plot and heat map visualizations. The CMDGA also continues to add new datasets and data types. Find details on their latest release here.

Focus groups

We’ve started a regular series of focus groups to help us gather input as we develop new tools and interfaces. These bimonthly sessions are held at the same time as our webinar series, in alternate months. Participants will receive a link to a prototype tool on our development site; they will test it beforehand and come to the session prepared for discussion. Join our Knowledge Portal mailing list to be invited to these sessions!

Translating biomedical results

NCATS Biomedical Translator is a large project that integrates multiple data sources with the goal of translating the results of basic biomedical research into accessible knowledge that can be applied to public health. Did you know that the Knowledge Portal team is involved in this project? We act as a Knowledge Provider for genetic information, contributing results distilled from the genetic association results in the Portals to suggest links between genes and diseases.

Join us at ADA!

The 82nd Scientific Sessions of the American Diabetes Association will take place on June 3-7 in New Orleans, LA and virtually. We’ll have both an in-person exhibit booth (#1410) and an ancillary session on June 3 that will also be broadcast as a webinar, as well as presenting a poster on the Type 1 Diabetes Knowledge Portal. Be sure to join our mailing list, or watch our home page or Twitter feed, for all the detailsm.
